MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION SPECIAL MEETING
  MONDAY, JULY 10, 2023

A special meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order by CHAIR YOO at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Yoo, Medawar, Olson, Romanelli, Nicklas, Schachter

  City Staff Present:  Jeannie Naughton, Community Development Director
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst

  Also Present:  Don Davis, City Attorney

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, JUNE 5, 2023.

COMMISSIONER OLSON made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES FOR THE MEETING OF JUNE
  5, 2023.

There being no objection, CHAIR YOO so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

NONE

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 230037; LOCATION: CITYWIDE; COMPREHENSIVE
  ZONING CODE UPDATE - COMMERCIAL DISTRICT

Community Development Director Naughton stated that staff is seeking direction on the type of
Land Uses that will be permitted by-right, conditionally permitted, or prohibited in the Commercial
District.

Director Naughton stated that at the last meeting, the planning commission asked staff to return
with occupancy ratings that are required for learning/tutorial centers. The California Building Code
requires 150 SF per person; the California Department of Education set guidelines based on
students’ age.

Director Naughton stated that currently applications for these types of uses are reviewed
ministerially if there are less than fifteen students or based on one-on-one sessions. Staff
presented the following options for consideration:

  •  Establish tenant space size as a determinant for requiring a CUP. It would limit the number
  of people occupying the tenant space at any given time and would allow for flexibility for
  student to teacher ratios.

  •  Establish a total number of students as a determinant for requiring a CUP. This could
  mean varying size tenant spaces, depending on the learning center’s teacher to student
  ratio.

VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR inquired how many learning/tutorial centers are in the city. Director
Naughton stated that there are about a dozen of these centers in the city.

CHAIR YOO asked about recreational uses that do not require a CUP where instruction is being

PLANNING COMMISSION SPECIAL MEETING
MINUTES, JULY 10, 2023
  1
 provided for sports versus instruction for education. Director Naughton stated that this is correct,
there is no limitation on recreational uses, which includes the size of the tenant space. Director
Naughton stated that tutoring/learning centers have little to no impact on smaller scale use. The
larger tutoring facilities may have operational impacts due to drop-off and traffic.

In response to a question by VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR, Director Naughton stated that these
centers typically have more activity after-school and may impact later p.m. peak traffic.

A brief discussion ensued regarding other “instructional” type uses as compared to
learning/tutorial uses.

VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR asked if there have been any code enforcement issues with
learning/tutorial centers. City Attorney Davis stated that there have not been any code
enforcement issues that have been brought to his attention.

Attorney Davis stated that he will be present at these meetings due to the substantive issues that
are coming up. He stated that the purpose of CUP’s is to give the Planning Commission discretion
when a particular use may create issues. Attorney Davis explained how uses could be regulated
by including additional standards in the code.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI inquired about using the Department of Education’s student to
teacher ratios. Director Naughton explained that this would be difficult to enforce.

Director Naughton stated that the building department would regulate the occupancy of the tenant
space. She stated that staff can look into the average tenant space size of the existing centers in
the city and bring this item back to the commission for final approval.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that there should be some consistency with other uses
within certain categories. He stated that there would need to be a reason for limiting particular
uses. CHAIR YOO stated that there should be the least restrictions for educational activities.

In response to a question by VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR, Director Naughton stated that currently in
the code learning/tutorial centers require a CUP regardless of size or number of students.

Director Naughton stated that there are inconsistencies in the code in regard to garden plants,
shrubs, and garden supplies. Staff presented the following options for consideration:

  •  Garden, plants, shrubs, and garden supplies be permitted for an established tenant size
  and/or outside area combined, that exceed this area, require a CUP.

  •  Eliminate the garden plants, shrubs, and garden supplies from the list of uses in the CG
  and CL District, since it is already addressed in other ways.

The commission agreed to eliminate this category.

Director Naughton stated that at the last meeting, the planning commission agreed that smaller
markets operate differently than the larger grocery stores and directed staff to provide thresholds
for requiring a CUP. Staff presented the following options for consideration:

  •  Establish a tenant space size threshold between 2,500 SF and 5,000 SF for
  markets/groceries as permitted uses.
  o Include delicatessens as permitted uses.
  o Allow limited seating as ancillary uses (no table service or on-site alcohol
  consumption).
  o Establish operational hours.

  •  Require a CUP for markets/groceries larger than 5,000 SF.
  o Required a CUP for table service dining (café use) and for any on-site alcohol
  consumption or tastings.

The commission agreed with the staff’s recommendation.

Director Naughton stated that the Planning Commission recommended that CUP be required for
restaurants and delicatessens. To align with the vision statement in the Land Use Element, staff
is requesting that the planning commission discuss and reconsider this requirement. Staff
presented the following options for consideration:

  •  Consider a threshold for triggering the need to require a CUP for restaurant use that is
  based on operational hours, alcohol licensing, or odor-producing activities.

PLANNING COMMISSION SPECIAL MEETING
MINUTES, JULY 10, 2023
  2
   •  Allow restaurants by right, that do not meet the chosen threshold(s) listed above.

A brief discussion ensued.

The Planning Commission agreed that restaurants should be encouraged and facilitate new
restaurants to be established in the city.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that there should be a square footage threshold in every
category requiring a CUP.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked how mixed-use would be addressed. Director Naughton
stated that alcohol licenses including operational hours would still require a CUP.

A brief discussion ensued.

The commission agreed with staff’s recommendation and added that beer and wine not be
restricted within predetermined operational hours. Director Naughton stated that she could bring
back a list of restaurants that do not currently have an alcohol license.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE

9.  COMMISSIONER ITEMS

COMMISSIONER OLSON asked about future planning issues considering the occurrence on
Peartree Lane.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR thanked the city for the street repaving on Silver Spur Road.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked if the Planning Commission could be included in what
caused the occurrence and will the commission be briefed.

City Attorney Davis stated that there will be meetings and discussion about this issue, and it will
be public information. He added that if the subdivision was done today, the standards would be
different. There was a meeting with the homeowners and there had been issues going on for two
months and it was being brought up to the homeowner’s association, but it was never elevated to
the city, sheriff’s, or fire department. As planning commissioners, if you hear of something similar,
direct the public to let someone know.

Director Naughton stated that the Planning Commission should direct residents to
www.rhe.city/peartreelane.

10.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

NONE

11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS – JUNE 13, 2023

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI
to,
  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEM 11A

There being no objection, CHAIR YOO so ordered.

11.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR YOO adjourned the meeting at 8:10 p.m.

The next Planning Commission meeting will be held on Monday, August 7, 2023 at 7:00 p.m.in
the City Hall Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates.

Respectfully submitted by,  Approved,

Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst  Victor Yoo, Chair
